newsitem.title: USA: Nets Inc files for Chapt. 11 bankruptcy protection.
newsitem.headline: Nets Inc files for Chapt. 11 bankruptcy protection.

text.p: Nets Inc, a startup focused on business-to-business electronic commerce, said Friday that it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection due to an inability to secure additional long-term financing.

The company, whose chairman is Jim Manzi, the former chief executive of Lotus Development Corp, said it will maintain its Industry.net service, as it examines its options for reorganizing the company under Chapter 11.
Manzi said in a statement that he personally provided bridge financing to the company in the past few weeks. Nets Inc is privately held.
A company spokesman said work on a reorganization plan starts next week.

Nets Inc, headquartered in Cambridge, Mass., had operations and a production facility in Pittsburgh and 200 employees. Nets Inc was formed through the merger of AT&T Corp's new media services and Industry.net in June 1995. The Industry.net service went live on the Web in September 1994, providing an electronic marketplace for buyers and sellers of industrial goods and services.
AT&T is a minority investor and Manzi owns less than five percent of the company.
Manzi stayed with Lotus Development for a few months after it was acquired in 1995 by International Business Machines Corp and later joined Industry.net.

"In the past few weeks, I've personally provided bridge financing to the company to provide us the opportunity to successfully execute the business concept," Manzi said in a statement. "But our financing deadline has passed and we do not have the capital to build from strength."
